clue.text: Reason behind player's obscure position

indicators.note: behind places the word for reason after the word for player

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in rugby or football
ground means reason, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: An explanation for why a footballer plays in some unglamorous spot on the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept in the background sits in an inconspicuous, out-of-sight place, an obscure position.

clue.text: Goldilocks, possibly, caught in flatter surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the flattery phrase encloses the caught letter

parts.note: to butter up is to flatter
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale girl is caught amid fawning admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: Goldilocks is not the fairy-tale girl but a woodland buttercup species, Ranunculus auricomus; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldilocks is the common name of a wild plant in the buttercup genus, so it is one example.

clue.text: Firm leading old print union a dance

indicators.note: leading puts the firm in front of the union

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
the NGA was the National Graphical Association, a British printing union

explanation.surface: A company heads a former printers' union in a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a single-file line.

clue.text: August issue gives shop-owner's description of Nell Trent

parts.note: august means grand, majestic
issue means offspring, such as a daughter

explanation.surface: An August edition of a magazine describes Dickens's Little Nell.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Trent is Little Nell of The Old Curiosity Shop, who lives with her grandfather, the shop's owner.
explanation.definitionFit: To the old man who keeps the curiosity shop, Nell is his son's child's child, his grandchild.

clue.text: Supervise, and risk eyestrain?

definitions.meaning: read as ..., to see too much and tire the eyes

explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise; split as over-see it jokingly means looking too much.

clue.text: Fellow upset boss in plant

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the fellow's name upside down

parts.note: Len is a man's name, standing for any fellow
an umbo is the boss in the centre of a shield

explanation.surface: A man upsets his manager in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a botanical plant; NELUMBO is the lotus genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelumbo is the botanical genus of the sacred lotus, a water plant.

clue.text: Petty quarrel in which light blows are returned

indicators.note: being returned sends the word for light blows back the other way

parts.note: taps are light blows

explanation.surface: A minor squabble where the participants trade gentle slaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief, trivial argument, a synonym for a petty quarrel.

clue.text: A soldier thus hangs on to it like a leech

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: hangs on to means the word for thus holds the word it within it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier clings to something as a leech would.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a classic parasite, living off its host, so behaving like one is parasitic.

clue.text: Current trends in fashionable diets

indicators.note: fashionable, read as able to be fashioned, signals the letters of diets being reshaped

explanation.surface: The latest crazes in trendy weight-loss regimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides are currents of opinion or events, as in the tide of fashion, so trends.

clue.text: Capacity of vessel taking horse in to tyneside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in tells us the horse word goes inside the two words that follow it

parts.note: Tyneside lies in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
a nag is a horse, usually an old one

explanation.surface: A ship's cargo capacity when it carries a horse to the north-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is the measure of a ship's carrying capacity, expressed in tons.

clue.text: Museum blind finally provided with overlapping slats

parts.note: the Louvre is the famous Paris museum

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word blind

explanation.surface: A museum's window blind has angled overlapping slats.
explanation.definitionFit: Louvred describes a door or window fitted with sloping slats that overlap to admit air but not rain.

clue.text: Blameless university member not initially willing to learn

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

indicators.note: not initially removes the first letter of the word for willing to learn

parts.note: teachable means willing or able to learn

explanation.surface: An eager, blameless academic is a member of a university.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpeachable means beyond reproach, so it is a synonym of blameless.

clue.text: One browses in the African plain, the Spanish also

definitions.text: One browses in the African plain

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine form of the
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Something grazing on the African savannah, with a Spanish word thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large antelope of the African grasslands that browses on leaves and shrubs.

clue.text: My boss is one that's wrecked a close relationship

indicators.note: wrecked tells us the letters of the preceding words are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A worker complains that their boss has ruined a close working relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link; 'wrecked' rearranges MYBOSSIS plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbiosis is a mutually dependent association, from biology, used for any close partnership.

clue.text: In which doctors can't abide giving treatment?

definitions.text: In which doctors can't abide giving treatment?

parts.words: In which doctors can't abide giving treatment?
parts.note: abide is read as reside rather than tolerate: a small rural hospital where local GPs treat patients but no doctors live in

explanation.surface: A hospital where physicians cannot bear the thought of treating anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: A COTTAGE HOSPITAL is a small British rural hospital without resident medical staff, served by visiting local GPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Such small country hospitals are staffed by visiting general practitioners rather than doctors living on site.

clue.text: Person causing suffering to soldiers in hills

indicators.note: in puts the soldiers between the two hills

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, so hills give two of them
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Someone inflicts pain on troops stationed in hilly country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is one who inflicts suffering on another.

clue.text: What a single lady may hope to do, being a steward?

definitions.text: What a single lady may hope to do
definitions.meaning: read as ..., to catch herself a husband
an agent who manages a landed estate

explanation.walkthrough: A LAND-AGENT manages a country estate for its owner, a British role once called a steward.
explanation.definitionFit: A land agent administers a landowner's estate, the job of an estate steward.

clue.text: Pickle beginning to chortle after chasing river bird?

indicators.note: chasing means the following pieces come behind the river, as a pursuer follows

parts.note: Peregrine Pickle is the hero of Smollett's novel, so Pickle stands for his first name
the Fal is a river in Cornwall

indicators.note: beginning to selects the first letter of chortle

parts.note: on can mean after, as in later on or from then on

explanation.surface: Someone pickled starts laughing after racing alongside a river bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickle looks like vinegar or a scrape but is Smollett's Peregrine Pickle; the question mark marks the falcon as a bird by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is a fast bird of prey, a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: One disregards resistance in troubled region

indicators.note: in puts the resistance symbol inside the rearranged region
troubled tells us the letters of region are stirred up

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone who ignores the opposition in a strife-torn area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns REGION into IGNOER; 'in' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorer is a person who disregards something, matching the definition as one who disregards.

clue.text: German city with English church Cologne, perhaps?

parts.note: Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr
CE, the Church of England

explanation.surface: A German city, an English church, and then Cologne, another German city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cologne looks like another German city but is eau de Cologne, a perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Cologne is a scent, and an essence is an extracted perfume, so it is an example.

clue.text: Insect attacks milk

definitions.meaning: the stings of a honey-making insect, read as two words
the first milk a cow gives after calving, colostrum

explanation.definitionFit: Beestings is the old word for the rich first milk from a cow that has just calved.

clue.text: Writer of essays got home successfully

definitions.meaning: Francis ..., author of the Essays of 1597
evokes the idiom brought home the meat that means succeeding or earning a living

explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon wrote the Essays, and bringing home the bacon is the idiom for succeeding.

clue.text: Monster featuring in trashy drama .

indicators.note: featuring in says the letters appear within the run trashy drama

explanation.surface: A monster appears in a cheap, sensational play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra is the many-headed serpent monster slain by Heracles in Greek myth.

clue.text: Seaweed Lowry initially placed in proper setting

indicators.note: setting means the word for proper surrounds the painter's initials, as a jewel is set

parts.note: due means proper, fitting, as in due respect
the painter L. S. Lowry's initials are L and S

explanation.surface: The artist Lowry places some seaweed in an appropriate background.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it gives Lowry's two initials, LS. 'placed in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulse is an edible red seaweed found on Atlantic coasts.

clue.text: One may bring in whip before end of dinner

parts.note: cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of dinner

explanation.surface: Someone cracks a whip just before the meal finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A food supplier is hired to bring in the meal for a function.

clue.text: Having run away, Jacob's eldest flies back across US city in the clouds

indicators.note: across means the turned name spans either side of the city
flies back turns the shortened son's name round
away, with having, says the run letter is removed

parts.note: Reuben was the firstborn of Jacob's twelve sons in Genesis
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Jacob's firstborn runs off and flies back over an American city among the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having run away' drops R from REUBEN, leaving EUBEN; 'flies back' makes NEBUE, which goes 'across' LA. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulae are interstellar clouds of gas and dust; the Latin word itself means mists or clouds.

clue.text: Spy that's a nuisance down under

definitions.meaning: a police informer, a copper's spy, in British slang
in Australian slang the word means an annoying person or spoilsport

explanation.definitionFit: Nark is British slang for an informer and Australian slang for an irritating killjoy.

clue.text: Disrespectful night-rider in Irish book

indicators.note: in places the rider's name inside the other two pieces

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a book of the Bible
Paul Revere made the famous midnight ride of 1775 to warn of the British

explanation.surface: An impudent nocturnal horseman appears in an Irish book.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent means lacking proper respect, a direct synonym of disrespectful.
